slides.headline: He built the first free webmail service the world actually used, then sold it for $400 million.
Sabeer Bhatia
slides.body: Born in Chandigarh, Bhatia moved to the US for engineering studies at Caltech and Stanford. In 1996, with co-founder Jack Smith, he launched Hotmail - one of the first free, web-based email services anyone could sign up for.

slides.headline: 18 months from launch to a $400 million sale.
slides.body: Hotmail grew fast enough that Microsoft came calling within two years of launch. On December 30, 1997, Bhatia sold the company to Microsoft for $400 million in stock - a landmark deal for an Indian-origin founder building outside India.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: India's growth story runs through its diaspora too.
slides.body: Millions of Indians have built careers, companies and inventions abroad since. Their success isn't separate from India's own growth - it's proof of what Indian talent can build anywhere, and increasingly, a source of capital and expertise flowing back home.
